hidden.d: Five blocks east of the Central Cathedral, this landmark church has an ornate Baroque style, even though it was built in 1941.
Alajuela's Central Cathedral is the very center of the town as is traditional in colonial Spanish urban planning. The church is pretty, but not a spectacular piece of architecture.

Alajuela is the hometown to Juan Santamaría, the Costa Rican National Hero. Around the city you can see the location of his home, although now there is just a small plaque and garden as the house in long gone.
A block north of the Central Park is the Juan Santamaría Museum, which shows some era pieces explaining the legacy of Juan Santamaría and the 1856 campaign against the filibuster invaders led by U.S.

x.intro: Alajuela is a city in the Central Valley of Costa Rica, near San José. It is not to be confused with Alajuela Province, which extends north from the city of Alajuela to North Costa Rica.

next.d: in Alajuela Province – It had been ranked as the best weather worldwide. Atenas town in well known by the American community here.

x.around: Cartago downtown is perhaps the smallest of the main cities in the Central Valley, it is possible to walk all around the city in short time.

hidden.d: A dam was built in the 1970s for hydroelectricity production, and the artificial lake is surrounded by beautiful mountains. Trout is cultivated in many places around the lake.
Beautiful view of Orosi valley.
Beautiful view of Orosi valley.
This is a place to buy wood crafts made from coffee roots.

As the legend goes, the Basilica was built on the exact site where a figurine of the Virgin Mary appeared to local native girl Juana Pereira in 1635, the girl brought the figurine to her house but it disappeared, without her…

n.en: Basílica de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles

hidden.d: A fun river to cross by foot, the locals ask for a collaboration, ₡1,000 or more is appropriate. If travelling in group by car, have the driver drop the group on the east side and then pick the rest of the group on the west side…
A church built by the Spanish colonists in 1743, still in use and carefully preserved. National monument.

n.en: Iglesia de San José de Orosi

hidden.d: A sanatorium built in 1918 by ex-president and physician Dr. Carlos Durán for tuberculosis patients. The place has been abandoned for years and the local farmers have taken care of it.

x.intro: For other places with the same name, see Cartago (disambiguation). Cartago is a city in Costa Rica's Central Valley. It used to be the national capital before that honor went to San José and is one of the few places in the country where more than a handful colonial era buildings have survived to the present day.

must.d: Around 30 km from downtown Cartago, this is one of the most famous volcanoes in Costa Rica. This now-dormant volcano erupted in 1963 when John F. Kennedy was visiting Costa Rica.
A national park with four hiking trails for all levels of difficulty, with beautiful views of El Salto waterfall, and it is possible to swim in the Grande de Orosi River.

East of downtown Cartago, this garden hosts the largest collection of orchids and epiphytes in Central America, they also have collections in open air of bromeliads, cacti, succulents, heliconians, bamboos, palms, ferns, a…
Ruins of an ancient church built by the Spanish conquistadors, very peaceful surroundings with a hot spring nearby.

next.d: via Curridabat, is about an hour to the west via the highway.

x.around: You can easily walk most places in Heredia, or take a cab ride which will cost less than ₡1,000.

hidden.d: A majestic waterfall on the route from Heredia to Sarapiquí through Barva, public access with no fare required but the parking space around the waterfall might be limited.
Managed by the local government of San Rafael canton, it is a public recreation park in the heights of San Rafael, a very accessible fee is required for entrance.
The old post office, still in use, give a glimpse of how the city looked back in its heyday.
The free-standing facade of a demolished building stands in front of what is apparently a parking lot.
A museum managed by the National Autonomous University (UNA), created to preserve and share the old customs of the late 19th century and early 20th century.
City council building.
Heredia's first high school. Occupies most of a whole block, beautiful architecture.

x.intro: The Heredia region of the Central Valley of Costa Rica offers much for the visitor in downtown Heredia, and in many of the towns around Heredia, particularly in the north mountains, like Barva, San Rafael, San Isidro, where there are many coffee plantations and fresh air year round.

cities.d: the Central Pacific coast's largest city, among incredibly biodiversity and natural beauty, famous surf spot

x.around: Transportation in and around Jacó is quite simple. The city is small enough, that walking from one end to the other is not an impossible feat. But when it's hot, or it's dark, there are always plenty of taxis to take you down the strip wherever you might want to go. The taxis in Jaco are red. Uber is also available in Jaco. There's a taxi stand by the main grocery store, Mas por Menos.

hidden.d: Spanish language school that offers group, private, surf and special courses such as the "crash course" for travellers (1 to 5 days). The school also offers cultural activities and excursions during the week to practice Spanish.

x.intro: Jacó is one of the two largest tourist towns on the Central Pacific Coast of Costa Rica. It is a surfing town with a 4-km long black sand beach and several local surf shops where you can get a board or sign up for lessons.

next.d: There are many photo opportunities travelling south along the Costanera, and many secluded beaches. If you continue an hour south you will eventually come to the National Park, Manuel Antonio.
A popular surfing beach 5 minutes South of Jaco.

n.es: Refugio de Vida Silvestre Playa Hermosa-Punta Mala

next.d: A beach town about 30 minutes South of Jaco.

x.safe: Buses are very popular places for thieves and pickpockets to steal luggage and backpacks from unsuspecting tourists. They may be stolen from the storage underneath the bus, but always keep an eye on your belongings inside the bus as well.

cities.d: location of Guanacaste Airport and gateway to the beaches of Guanacaste, such as Samara, Nosara, Carillo

x.around: Public bus or on foot. Liberia is a small city where everything you are likely to wish to see is within walking distance.

hidden.d: Safari with African species, kayaking, waterfalls, zip-lines.
Town square in front of the Central Church of Liberia.
Housed in old city barracks, this museum is designed to relate information and history about the area. Kind of modest.
Museum about cowboy culture in Guanacaste province.

x.intro: Liberia is the capital city of the Guanacaste province of Costa Rica. It is located about 220 km (138 mi) Northwest San Jose.

intro: Costa Rica has bewilderingly diverse culture, climates, flora, and fauna, and landscapes range from rainforests, to dry tropical and temperate forests, to volcanoes, to Caribbean and Pacific beaches, to high mountains, and marshy lowlands. Costa Rica is an exceptionally stable and peaceful country compared to the volatile region it's in, and is one of the world's top destinations for nature and ecotourism.

hidden.d: 16 hot springs of various temperatures. Like Tabacon Hot Springs, this too is often included in volcano viewing packages.
More relaxing and a bit more discreet than either Baldi & Tabacon. Reservations definitely recommended as they limit to 100 guests. Good dinner and drinks.

A visit to the Butterfly Conservatory offers a practical educational experience about nature with diversified exhibits of how butterflies, frogs, insects, and plants are reproduced in this natural environment.
Take a dip in the refreshing waters of Río Fortuna and use the El Salto Rope Swing to jump into the water.

The fee includes modern changing rooms with locks, towels, and access to the multi-level hot spring with a slide, artificial waterfalls, view of the volcano, and bars for drinks without leaving the water.
This hike takes you through very dense primary forest toward the Cerro Chato. There is a crater lake where you can swim, take pictures and explore the surroundings.

x.intro: La Fortuna de San Carlos is a small town in the north of Costa Rica. It is known mainly for the nearby Arenal Volcano (1,633 m), a destination for scientists and tourists. See volcanoes for general information.

must.d: The photos at the right of this article are views from the village of El Castillo, on the southwest side of the Volcano, about 25 west of La Fortuna and about 4 up the road from the Arenal National Park entrance.

Just west of the Arenal Volcano and can be seen as you drive over the dam on the main highway to Tilaran. Much better views of the lake and volcano can be seen from the hills above the village of El Castillo, which is located 9…

Stone steps lead to the bottom. Take a swimsuit for the pool in the lovely stream below. The entrance is accessible by road, so a cab works fine too. Once you pay to go in, you are free to stay as long as you'd like.

x.safe: As of Feb 2019, those of you who catch the 8AM bus to Tilarán, be aware that every morning at the bus station there is a man talking nicely to the tourists and getting on the same bus. 4 before the National Park's bus stop, this man shouts "Parque Ecológico" and some tourists, who are confused, get off with him.

x.around: By foot. The park is not very big and can be circled within a few hours. There are several guides but use them to point out nature attractions since there is only one very well marked trail.
x.intro: Cahuita National Park is in eastern Costa Rica, along the Caribbean coast. The park is known for its pristine coral reef, turquoise waters, white sand beaches, and inland forests teeming with wildlife.
x.safe: Allow time to get back into town before dark. You wouldn't want to be lost in the jungle at night. Don't forget: it gets dark early.

x.around: Following the main trail will take up to 12 hours in poor conditions for slow hikers. Fit or experienced hikers may complete it in 6-7 hours. Follow the sign that says "Trail to Chirripo" and begin the La Cuesta del Agua uphill stretch for 2 hours. The climb crests at Monte Sin Fe. Finish the trek for the day at the Chirripo Shelter and Base Camp, 6 km below the summit.
x.intro: Parque Nacional Chirripó (Chirripó National Park) is a national park in South Pacific Costa Rica accessible by road through the locality of San Isidro de El General in Pérez Zeledón canton.

next.d: Walk down to the exit and take the bus back.

x.safe: It is best not to hike alone, and recommended to go with a local guide. The weather conditions can create an extreme (and cold) environment on the top of the peak and having a knowledgeable guide can be an asset in an emergency. Adventure Life offers guided 3- and 4-day packages with accommodations at Pelicano Lodge before and after the summit.

x.around: Getting around the island is a little tricky. The main types of transportation are by foot or bike usually used for hikes and sight-seeing tours. The few locals who live here mainly use foot, or bike, or small motor bikes and dirt bikes.
x.intro: Cocos Island is a nationally protected jungle-covered island and national park off the coast of Costa Rica. The park also includes surrounding ocean surface of about 60,000 square miles that were added to the park to protect several species of shark. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
x.safe: The only possible dangers in Cocos Island are the sharks, eels, and other creatures that might be seen while diving, snorkeling, boating, or fishing.
